description:
Runs from one sweep, or from every sweep this person has, filtered and sorted by the engine. LEAVE experiment_id OUT to search them all, which is how a person asking whether they have already found something like this gets an answer without spending a new search on a question that already has one. A SWEEP HAS NO WINNER: which run matters depends entirely on what was being asked, so you choose sort_by for the question in front of you -- return, risk-adjusted return, drawdown, trade count -- and say which one you sorted by whenever you report an order. Never call the top row 'the best strategy'; it is the top row by the measure you picked. Filter before you sort: a run with a handful of trades has metrics that mean nothing, so min_trades is usually the first thing to set. Every numeric filter has BOTH bounds, so a band is one question: a delta against the benchmark between 3 and 8 is min and max together, not a page fetched and thinned by hand. Readable while the sweep is still running.

[Access: pay 0.005 USDC via x402 (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header) OR authenticate with an API key. An x402-capable client will auto-pay; API-key clients pay nothing per call.]

asset.description: Asset symbol, e.g. BTC or ETH.

atr_period.description: Only runs that used this ATR period. Needs experiment_id.

beats_benchmarks.description: Only runs that beat all three benchmarks over the same

beats_crypto_benchmarks.description: Only runs that beat the crypto benchmarks rather than only their own asset.

candle_size.description: Duration of one candle, e.g. 1h or 1d.

cooldown_bars.description: Only runs that used this cooldown. Needs experiment_id.

covering.description: Only runs over windows covering this single date, as YYYY-MM-DD. A different question from a span.

covering_from.description: Only runs whose window OVERLAPS this date onwards. A run is relevant to 2024 if any of it happened in 2024.

covering_to.description: Only runs whose window overlaps up to this date.

experiment_id.description: The sweep, as create_sweep returned it.

generation.description: Only runs from this engine generation, so runs made under different engine behaviour are not compared as though alike.

market_direction.description: Only runs from windows of this market character, e.g. bear or mega_bull. Several are one comma-separated string, e.g. "bull,super_bull", and a run matching any of them counts. What a run did in one kind of market says little about another.

max_delta_vs_asset.description: Only runs beating their own asset by at most this much.

max_delta_vs_benchmark.description: Only runs beating their benchmark by at most this much, so "between 3 and 8" is one question rather than a page fetched and thrown away.

max_irr.description: Only runs at or below this annualised IRR.

max_return.description: Only runs at or below this total return.

max_risk_per_trade.description: Only runs that risked this fraction per trade. Needs experiment_id.

max_sharpe.description: Only runs at or below this Sharpe ratio.

max_trades.description: Only runs at or below this trade count. Pairs with min_trades to ask for a band rather than a floor.

max_win_rate.description: Only runs at or below this win rate.

min_delta_vs_asset.description: Only runs beating buy-and-hold on their own asset by at least this much.

min_delta_vs_benchmark.description: Only runs that beat their benchmark by at least this much. A return in a rising market is not skill.

min_irr.description: Only runs at or above this annualised IRR.

min_return.description: Only runs at or above this total return.

min_sharpe.description: Only runs at or above this Sharpe ratio.

min_trades.description: Drop runs with fewer trades than this. Metrics from a handful of trades are noise.

min_win_rate.description: Only runs at or above this win rate.

offset.description: Pagination offset in the result units documented by the tool; zero starts the first page.

order.description: desc for best-first on that metric, asc for worst-first.

regime_composite.description: Only runs from windows with this full regime label, e.g. mega_bull_high_clean, when the three parts together matter; several comma-separated, any of them counts. Across different regime filters every one must hold.

regime_direction.description: The direction band from get_market_regime, e.g. bear. The signal searches filter by it and find_sweep_runs marks each row's regime_fit with it; save_strategy and update_strategy read the current band themselves, so their check runs without it.

reward_factor.description: Only runs that used this reward-to-risk setting. Execution filters need experiment_id; the cross-sweep surface does not serve them.

run_index.description: Which run, as find_sweep_runs reported it.

run_status.description: Only runs with this outcome, e.g. no_trades for the ones that never opened a position.

sort_by.description: The metric to order by, e.g. sharpe_ratio, sortino_ratio, irr_annualized, total_return, max_drawdown, total_trades. Required, because the choice IS the question being asked.

trend.description: Only runs from windows of this trend character, e.g. clean or choppy; several comma-separated, any of them counts.

trigger_name.description: Only runs whose entry trigger is this signal.

volatility.description: Only runs from windows of this volatility band, e.g. low; several comma-separated, any of them counts.

name: find_sweep_runs
